insights.title: Exam anxiety the parent may not see

student_said.summary: Agrees that the mind goes blank before exams and that worry about marks makes it hard to concentrate (test anxiety high)

parent_said.summary: Describes the child as calm before exams

insights.meaning: Large gap on test anxiety: the student carries stress the parent does not notice. This is context for the session, not a diagnosis.
suggestions: Open the session with the student alone and ask how exams feel
Teach one short exam-routine (planning, breathing, sleep) and agree a follow-up date
If the student describes hopelessness or panic, follow the school's escalation protocol
talking_points: Many students feel more exam pressure than they show
Calm preparation helps marks more than extra hours
insights.avoid: Do not share the anxiety score with parents without the student's consent; do not use medical labels.

insights.title: Parents prefer Business and Medicine; student fits Animals and Environment

student_said.summary: Top fits: Animals and Veterinary (78), Environment (74). Own dream: veterinary work

parent_said.summary: Parent 1 prefers Medicine; Parent 2 prefers Business, which ranks 8th for this student

insights.meaning: Medicine is in the student's top 5, so one parent's wish is partly aligned. Business is not.
suggestions: Show the fit scores for Medicine, Business and Veterinary side by side
Explore the shared entrance route for MBBS and BVSc (verify the exam rules for the current year)
Ask each parent what outcome they most want: income, status or security, then match options to that
talking_points: The child is strong in science, so the medical-science family of courses is open
Your child's interest in animals is a strength worth building on, with real paths
insights.avoid: Do not tell parents their preference is wrong.

insights.title: High income worry on the student's top fields

student_said.summary: Values Helping first and Money 7th of 8

parent_said.summary: Worry about income is high for Animals (4.6) and Environment (4.3)

insights.meaning: The concern is about earning, not about the child's ability.
suggestions: Bring the verified earning ladder (entry, 5-year, 10-year) for veterinary, wildlife and animal nutrition roles; data is pending for this build
Show specialisations and private-practice or research routes with higher income
Compare course cost against likely return
talking_points: Let us look at what people in these fields actually earn at each stage
insights.avoid: Do not quote salaries without a verified source.

insights.title: Strong nature interest the parents have barely noticed

student_said.summary: Love for observing nature and identifying birds and plants; loses track of time doing so

parent_said.summary: Few nature behaviours seen in early years or now (observed 40)

insights.meaning: The interest may be expressed outside the parents' sight.
suggestions: Ask the student to show a photo journal, trek or garden project
With consent, share the concrete evidence with the parents
Suggest one low-cost trial such as a nature club or wildlife volunteering
talking_points: Your child does this on their own time, which is a sign of real interest
insights.avoid: Do not call the parents inattentive.

insights.title: Parent sees a talent for teaching and guiding that the student ranks low

student_said.summary: Low interest in Education and Psychology (42) but good empathy score (74)

parent_said.summary: Strong early and current helping behaviour; teachers praise helping classmates (76)

insights.meaning: A strength that does not match the student's current interests.
suggestions: Ask what the student thinks about the teacher comments
Suggest peer-tutoring or mentoring for a term as a low-pressure test
Keep it as a supporting skill for veterinary or public-health careers
talking_points: This is a strength you may use in any career, not a different career you must choose
insights.avoid: Do not push it as an alternative to the student's own interest.

insights.title: Parent rates maths higher than the test shows

student_said.summary: Numerical aptitude is moderate (55); logical is strong (72)

parent_said.summary: Rates the child much stronger than peers in maths (80)

insights.meaning: Logical strength supports science; numerical skill may need building for competitive exams.
suggestions: Show the logical strength as evidence the child can do science
Offer a 6-month practice plan for numerical speed before entrance exams
Review recent maths marks together
talking_points: The child is good at reasoning; speed with numbers can be trained
insights.avoid: Do not compare with siblings or classmates.

insights.title: The two parents want different careers
insights.meaning: The child may feel pulled in two directions.
suggestions: Run a joint session and agree the criteria first: interest, ability, income, location
Then compare options against those criteria
talking_points: Let us first agree what a good outcome looks like for your child
insights.avoid: Do not take sides between the parents.

insights.title: Parents think the child values money more than the child does

parent_said.summary: Expects Money and Security to matter most

insights.meaning: Different assumptions about what a good career is.
suggestions: Ask the student to explain their values in their own words to the parents
talking_points: Your child cares about helping people and animals
insights.avoid: Do not dismiss the parents' security concerns.

red_flags: High test anxiety reported by the student; parent unaware. Arrange a follow-up conversation.

session_plan.goal: Explain that the report is a conversation starter, not a verdict
Check exam anxiety, hear their own words on animals and nature
Understand what outcome they want: income, status, security
Walk through the map; compare Veterinary, Medicine and Environment routes
Agree a trial activity, a numerical practice plan and a follow-up date

data_gaps: Verified earning ladder not supplied for Animals and Environment (data pending)
Norms are provisional for this grade
Entrance-exam rules must be verified for the current year
counsellor_summary: Student and parents agree on science, but the parents are split between Medicine and Business while the student is drawn to animals and nature. The main gaps are exam anxiety the parents do not see and a worry about income. A shared science route and verified earning data can bridge the views.
